





                               DRIFTWOOD

                 A Card Game of Tides, Boats and Cargo

                                 Rules

                            For two players



Contents

1. Components ............................................. 3
2. Zones .................................................. 3
3. Setup .................................................. 4
4. The Turn ............................................... 5
5. Boats and Cargo ........................................ 6
6. Squalls and the Tide ................................... 7
7. Winning and Variants ................................... 8
8. Clarifications ......................................... 8
9. Solo Play .............................................. 8

                                 - 2 -

1.      Components

1.1     Driftwood is a card game for two players.

1.2     The deck holds fifty-four cards of three kinds: Boat cards,
        Cargo cards and Squall cards.

1.3     Every Boat card shows a capacity. Every Cargo card shows a
        weight. Squall cards show neither.

1.4     A tide marker rests on a track of five marks, numbered one to
        five, between the two players.

2.      Zones

2.1     The Stock is a shared pile of face-down cards. No player may
        look at it, and its order is kept.

2.2     A player's Hand holds cards that only that player may look at.
        The order of cards in a Hand does not matter.

2.3     A player's Harbour is the area in front of that player where
        boats lie face up. Cargo loaded onto a boat lies on that boat,
        face up.

2.4     The Wreck pile is a shared pile of face-up cards. The card
        placed most recently lies on top.

2.5     If the Stock is empty when a card must be drawn, shuffle the
        Wreck pile and turn it face down to form a new Stock.


                                 - 3 -

3.      Setup

3.1     The winner of a coin toss chooses who takes the first turn and
        must announce the choice before cards are dealt. If the winner
        is unsure, they may let the other player decide.

3.2     Shuffle all fifty-four cards to form the Stock.

3.3     Each player draws five cards from the Stock to form an opening
        Hand.

3.4     Place the tide marker on mark one.


                                 - 4 -

4.      The Turn

4.1     A turn has four phases, taken in this order: Ebb, Sail, Flood
        and Moor. The player whose turn it is, the active player, takes
        all four.

4.2     In the Ebb phase the active player draws cards from the Stock
        until holding five cards in their Hand.

4.3     In the Sail phase the active player may take any number of the
        actions in section 5, in any order.

4.4     In the Flood phase the tide rises by one mark. Then the
        slack-water window opens. Each player, starting with the player
        who is not active, may play one Squall card or pass. The window
        closes when both players have passed in succession.

4.5     In the Moor phase the active player discards cards from their
        Hand until holding at most seven.

4.5a    The turn then passes to the other player, who begins again at
        the Ebb phase.


                                 - 5 -

5.      Boats and Cargo

5.1     To launch a boat, the active player discards one card from their
        Hand and moves a Boat card from their Hand to their Harbour.

5.1a    A player may launch at most two boats in each turn.

5.2     The active player may move a Cargo card from their Hand onto a
        boat in their Harbour. A boat may carry any number of Cargo
        cards.

5.3     Whenever the combined weight of the cargo on a boat is greater
        than that boat's capacity, that boat is wrecked. A wrecked boat
        and all of its cargo go to the Wreck pile. If several boats are
        overloaded at the same moment, all of them are wrecked together.

5.4     A boat that carries at least one Cargo card may sail out. The
        owner scores points equal to the weight aboard. A boat carrying
        3 units of weight scores 3 points. Its cargo then goes to the
        Wreck pile and the boat returns to its owner's Hand.

5.5     Example: A boat has capacity four and carries cargo of weight
        two and weight one. The owner loads a cargo of weight two. The
        total is now five, which is more than four, so the boat is
        wrecked together with all three Cargo cards.


                                 - 6 -

6.      Squalls and the Tide

6.1     The tide rises by moving the marker up one mark. When the marker
        would move past mark five, it goes back to mark one.

6.2     During the slack-water window a player may play a Squall card
        from their Hand and choose one boat in the other player's
        Harbour. That boat is beached.

6.3     A beached boat loses all of its cargo, which goes to the Wreck
        pile. The boat itself stays in its Harbour.

6.4     A boat marked Buoyant cannot be beached.

6.5     While the marker is on mark five, a beached boat keeps its cargo
        and the Squall goes to the Wreck pile instead.

6.6     While the marker is on mark five, the capacity of every boat
        counts as one higher.

6.7     When a boat is launched, its owner looks at the top card of the
        Stock.

6.7a    That look is taken at the start of the following Flood phase,
        not at the moment of launch.


                                 - 7 -

7.      Winning and Variants

7.1     Driftwood has two formats: the Short Tide and the Full Tide.

7.2     In the Short Tide a player wins on reaching ten points. In the
        Full Tide a player wins on reaching twenty points.

8.      Clarifications

8.1     No player may end a turn holding more than seven cards.

8.2     When a Squall is played against a Buoyant boat, nothing happens
        to the boat and the Squall still goes to the Wreck pile.

8.3     The marker stays on mark five once it arrives there.

9.      Solo Play

9.1     One person may play against an automated opponent.

9.2     On the automated opponent's turn, reveal the top card of the
        Stock and follow the table printed on that card.

9.3     The automated opponent never plays Squall cards.

9.4     The automated opponent never launches more than one boat in a
        turn.


                                 - 8 -
